headings.title: Service of appointed commissioners until election
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Covers appointed commissioners serving until successors are duly elected and qualified; distinct from elected members' terms in subsection 3.

headings.title: Elected commissioner terms, staggering, and term limit
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Covers elected commissioners drawing lots at their first meeting for initial 2-, 4-, and 6-year terms followed by 6-year terms, holdover until successor qualification, and a limit of two terms whether partial or full.

headings.title: Filling vacancies and meeting per diem
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Covers county commissions filling vacancies from their counties for unexpired terms and members receiving a commission-set per diem for attending commission meetings.

headings.title: Commissioner oath of office
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note. Covers each commission member taking and subscribing an oath before entering official duties before an officer authorized to administer oaths.

headings.title: Election and qualifications of president and secretary
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1992 S.B. 661 & 620 §§ 25, 26, A.L. 1993 H.B. 482). Covers choosing a commissioner as president at the first meeting and electing a secretary (a resident of a district county, who may or may not be a commissioner) to serve until a successor is appointed and qualified.

headings.title: Commission seal and public proceedings record
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Covers permissive adoption of a seal and mandatory keeping of a proceedings record open to inspection by all interested parties.

headings.title: Majority voting and equal commissioner votes
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Covers requiring majority vote for any commission action and giving each commissioner one vote.

headings.title: Mandatory commission duties and agency information sharing
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 including subdivisions (1) through (5) and history note. headings.title: Permissive commission powers and rulemaking
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 including subdivisions (1) through (8) and history note. Covers permissive ('may') commission authority to hold hearings, classify water, initiate studies, set well-spacing/quality criteria and recommendations, contract, accept and budget grants/funds, adopt rules after public notice and hearings, and represent the district before state and federal agencies; contrasted with mandatory duties in subsection 4.

headings.title: Preservation of well installation board authority
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and history note. Covers the rule of construction stating that nothing in subsections 4 to 6 of section 256.653 limits the powers, duties, or authority of the well installation board under sections 256.600 to 256.640; explicitly retains the archived self-referential range 'subsections 4 to 6 of this section' without altering source wording.

headings.title: Annual irrigation well fees and voter-approved increases
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1992 S.B. 661 & 620 § 27, A.L. 1993 H.B. 482). headings.title: Fees for drilling or plugging irrigation wells
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Covers mandatory $15 fees payable to the commission by owners of 6-inch-or-greater irrigation wells for each new well drilled and each well plugged under chapter 256.

headings.title: Quarterly and called commission meetings
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Covers requiring the commission to meet at least quarterly and upon call of the president or any three commission members; distinct from fee provisions in surrounding subsections.

headings.title: Fee exemption for political subdivisions and special districts
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Covers exempting any political subdivision or special district of the state from fees authorized under section 256.655.

headings.title: Secretary serving as district treasurer
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 1992 S.B. 661 & 620 § 28). Covers designating the commission secretary as district treasurer responsible for receiving and receipting all moneys collected or obtained by the commission.

headings.title: Secretary compensation, office, equipment, and records
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Covers permissive commission-fixed monthly salary and necessary expenses for the secretary, furnishing office space and specified supplies/equipment in a district county, and keeping district records in that office.

headings.title: Appointment and payment of deputy secretaries
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Covers permissive appointment of one or more deputies by the secretary with commission advice and consent, with salaries and necessary expenses paid by the district.

headings.title: Secretary official bond and custody
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Covers commission-fixed bond with at least two sureties or a commission-approved surety/bonding company, in addition to any bond for bond-sale proceeds, held in the commission president's custody separate from the secretary's papers.

headings.title: Depositing district funds and crediting interest
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note. Covers depositing all funds received by the secretary in commission-designated bank(s) or trust company and crediting all accrued interest to the district.

headings.title: Annual audit, landowner report, and county clerk filing
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and history note. Covers annual certified public accountant audit of the secretary's books, reporting receipts, disbursements, and beginning/ending balances to landowners within 30 days thereafter, and filing a copy with the county clerk of each county containing district land.

headings.title: Disbursing funds by signed warrants and warrant form
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 7 including the embedded statutory warrant-form table and history note. Covers restricting disbursements to district warrants signed by the commission president and attested by the secretary, and sets out the prescribed tabular warrant form.

headings.title: Initiating disincorporation by commission or voter petition
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 including subdivisions (1) and (2) and history note (L. 1992 S.B. 661 & 620 § 29). Covers voter-approved disincorporation initiated either by commission determination within 30 days after a published-notice hearing or by a validated petition of at least 5% of qualified voters from each of a majority of district counties followed by a hearing and submission by county clerks absent withdrawal.

headings.title: Withdrawal of disincorporation petition before hearing ends
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Covers permissive withdrawal of a disincorporation petition by a majority of petitioners at any time before conclusion of the hearing to terminate proceedings.

headings.title: Form of disincorporation ballot question
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 including its continuation ballot-text paragraph and history note. Covers the substantially prescribed ballot question asking whether the Southeast Missouri Regional Water District shall be disincorporated.

headings.title: Majority vote required for disincorporation
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Covers requiring a majority of those voting on the question to approve disincorporation.

headings.title: Receiver appointment, powers, and termination of commissioners
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note. Covers certifying disincorporation to the court, court appointment of a district resident as receiver with corporate-liquidation receiver powers as a district officer, and terminating commissioners' authority and offices subject to court liquidation-aid orders.

headings.title: Distributing remaining funds and filing district records
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 including subdivisions (1) and (2) and history note. Covers the receiver's post-debt obligations subject to court orders to distribute remaining funds pro rata to each county commission based on last full year's district fee collections and to file official data, plans, and records with the court clerk as public records.

headings.title: Definitions for community geographical information systems
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 including subdivisions (1) through (3) and paragraphs (2)(a)–(c), plus history note (L. 1995 H.B. 452, et al. § 3). Covers section-scoped definitions of 'Community', 'Geographical information system', and 'Municipality' (city with 350,000 or more inhabitants located in more than one county).

headings.title: Policy on public access and special private benefit
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 2 and history note. Covers legislative policy that non-closed community geographical information system data should be publicly available while access turning public system investment into a special private benefit rather than a public benefit should not be permitted.

headings.title: Community creation and governance of the system
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 3 and history note. Covers permissive authority for a defined community to create a geographical information system and governing-body determination of scope, creation, maintenance, use, and distribution.

headings.title: Public disclosure, closed records, and computer-readable formats
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Covers barring withholding of collected/assimilated information unless properly closed under section 610.021, qualified by no obligation to disclose in computer-readable or manipulable form absent a license agreement.

headings.title: Disclosure fees, map products, and system licensing costs
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 including subdivisions (1) through (3) and history note. Covers section 610.026 reasonable fees for non-computer-readable disclosures, public availability and cost-capped fees for maps and products, and permissive system licensing reflecting production cost, creation/acquisition cost, and commercial-purpose value.

headings.title: Protected routine data collection and software licensing
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 6 and history note. Covers protecting daily or routine data collection (as defined in section 569.093) by listed real estate, title, development, surveying, utility, banking, and mortgage entities from hindrance and capping fees at section 610.026 levels, while permitting community licensing and cost-setting for the system's computer program and computer software (section 569.093); revised title clarifies protection rather than limits on collection.

headings.title: Community immunity for system or information errors
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 7 and history note. Covers shielding a community distributing geographical information system information or the system itself from damages liability arising from any error in the information or system.

headings.title: Annual geologic resources fee and small gravel exemption
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 1 and history note (L. 2007 S.B. 54, A.L. 2019 S.B. 84, A.L. 2023 S.B. 109). headings.title: Fee effective date and December 31, 2031 expiration
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Covers the August 28, 2007 effective date and December 31, 2031 expiration date for fees imposed under section 256.700, expressly providing that no other provisions of sections 256.700 to 256.710 expire.

headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 5 and history note. headings.title: State residency and reappointment eligibility
headings.reviewNote: Read complete text of subsection 4 and history note. Covers requiring all council members to be Missouri residents and permitting reappointment.
